title: Polyglot plotting gallery evidence
objective: Replace Wolfram and MATLAB plotting gallery placeholders with deterministic frontend-produced PlotSpec and Plotly fixtures plus structural responsive, accessibility, static export, and performance evidence

oracles: Integrated Wolfram and MATLAB frontend evaluation with semantic PlotSpec and Plotly output
Checked geometry, responsive, contrast, alt-text, SVG, and PNG evidence

handoff.summary: Replaced all Wolfram/MATLAB pending placeholders with 3 live frontend-produced fixtures, for 13 gallery fixtures total. The generator executes createSage.evaluate, captures actual PlotSpec/Plotly output and provenance, checks contrast and semantic bounds, records responsive Chromium geometry plus representative SVG/PNG structure, and keeps output compact without raster blobs or pixel hashes. Wolfram Axes->False is explicit and asserted in the rendered layout. Focused deterministic generation, live Chromium, architecture, and strict-baselib receipts pass on rebased main-2 at 8a2e2ce8.
risks: Wolfram and MATLAB currently generate useful semantic descriptions but do not attach explicit alt_text annotations; the fixtures intentionally retain PLOT_ALT_TEXT_MISSING.
Plotly's rendered DOM still lacks an accessible name, and visual aesthetics/keyboard behavior remain part of the documented human review protocol.
The Wolfram 3D frontend currently exposes a raw plotly-trace layer, so its bounds evidence is derived from the actual Plotly coordinate grids rather than semantic PlotSpec bounds.
Static export and live responsive evidence were recorded on linux-x64; the lane does not claim cross-platform Chromium execution.
next_steps: Run the broad pnpm test:integration tier in the root integration lane; it is intentionally not duplicated in this narrow evidence lane.
Promote foreign-frontend generated descriptions into explicit PlotSpec annotations and attach accessible naming in the renderer before claiming complete screen-reader support.
Use the documented human review protocol for a plotting release or Plotly/theme/default change.
